issues.description: Method name mismatch for Stock inventory-clearing operation: the problem statement UML declares a method Stock.emptyStock(): void (problem_statement.md lists +emptyStock() at line 54), the solution implementation provides Stock.emptyStock() (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java defines emptyStock()), but the template implementation exposes the same functionality under a different identifier Stock.clearInventory() (template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java defines clearInventory()). This naming inconsistency between template and specification/solution can confuse students (they will look for emptyStock() per the UML/spec or tests but only find clearInventory() in the starter code) and may cause tests or student code that call emptyStock() to fail to compile or run against the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (update its signature and body to public void emptyStock()) and update any internal/template references. This aligns the starter code with the UML and the solution, preventing confusion and compilation/test mismatches. Alternatively, if instructors prefer clearInventory(), update the problem statement UML and solution to declare and implement clearInventory() and mention the accepted name in the description.

issues.description: The concept is clearing the stock inventory. The problem statement (and the UML) requires a Stock method named emptyStock(), and the solution implementation provides Stock.emptyStock(). However, the template Stock class defines a method named clearInventory() instead of emptyStock(). This naming mismatch (emptyStock() vs clearInventory()) prevents students from directly matching the required API to the provided template, may cause compilation or test failures, and forces learners to reconcile two different identifiers for the same action.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a new public emptyStock() method in the template that delegates to clearInventory(). This makes the template, problem statement, and solution use the same method name (emptyStock) and avoids confusion or test/compilation issues.
